evidence_quotes.two_concerns_question: Never asked. Rep went directly into pricing explanation with no discovery of customer concerns.
evidence_quotes.two_layers_deep: N/A — no concerns were elicited because the two-concerns question was never asked.
evidence_quotes.value_days: Rep mentions 'November 3rd we can be able to book her site as early as 8:30 AM to 9:00 AM' but does not offer an alternative cheaper day, does not frame it as a Value Day choice, and does not ask about date flexibility.
evidence_quotes.rate_lock_then_ask: Rep said 'there's no deposit record no rested securing your spot' (rate lock / no deposit) but then immediately asked 'Would you like me to lock that in for you?' — the ask came with the rate lock at the same moment, not after, and the customer declined saying price was out of budget. No secondary ask for the business was made after the customer objected.

top_strength: Rep delivered both major promises (On-Time Guarantee with specific discount structure and No Worries Damage Coverage with $2,000 limit, no deductible, included in rate) clearly and early in the call.
coaching_note: This call skipped the entire Step 2 discovery — no two-concerns question, no probing into what mattered to Ruby, and no active listening — which meant the promises and estimate landed without context. Start every call with the two-concerns question before moving to pricing, and dig two layers deep on what Ruby cares about so the estimate answers her actual concerns, not just her square footage.
